extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, institutional grants administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update digest from NIH about policies, resources, and reminders relevant to applying for and managing NIH extramural grants. Intended to inform investigators and administrators about new formats, review process changes, and topical initiatives (e.g., reproducibility, DMS plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential while investigators remain responsible for choosing the model(s) best matched to their hypotheses and aims. (From: "Selecting the Right Models for Your Research: A Focus on New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)")

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PF5 overview to learn application format and award linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The video summarizes key features and the application format applicants should follow for PF5; it also explains administrative actions that may occur after review (e.g., splitting into linked awards). (From: "New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5)")

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH issued the 2026 Pilot format to streamline required elements for DMS Plans — applicants preparing DMS Plans should follow the new simplified format. (From: "2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan Format Available")

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and awards should reflect attention to replication and reproducibility; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative aim to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH emphasizes reliability of biomedical research as foundational; applicants should consider how their proposed work addresses replication/reproducibility and whether to engage with the Highlighted Topic. (From: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic")

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, applications in the middle third of a study section were designated as “competitive but not discussed,” recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects study section triage/cutoff procedures implemented after resumption of activities; the designation indicates competitiveness without being discussed at full review. (From: "My Application Was Scored as Competitive But Not Discussed During Review. What Does This Mean?")

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of centralized peer review changes and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) beginning March 2025; applicants should be aware this consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to peer review structure may affect assignment, review processes, and timeline expectations; applicants and institutional staff should monitor related guidance and notices. (From: "One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency")
